It doesn't use HTTP status codes, response objects, framework types, persistence or logging, so it carries no infrastructure or presentation responsibility. It holds no business rules that would belong in the domain either. It just reads the error's existing kind and message. This gives infrastructure adapters, such as the HTTP error-handling middleware, a simple contract to call, so they can report errors without knowing the concrete error types.
